### Hallador Reports Q3 2026 Results; Turtle Creek Advances Toward Year-End Final Investment Decision


November 9, 2026


*– Contracted Forward Sales Increase* 26% *from Q2’26 to* $3.0 billion *1* *at the Segment Level –*


*– Management Targets Approximately $1.6 Billion of Value from Turtle Creek Within 24 Months –*


TERRE HAUTE, Ind., Nov. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Hallador Energy Company (Nasdaq: HNRG) (“Hallador” or the “Company”) today reported its financial and operating results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. The Company is also providing an update on Turtle Creek Gas (“Turtle Creek”), its approximately 460-megawatt natural gas-fired generation project at the Merom site, which the Company is advancing toward a final investment decision (“FID”) targeted before the end of 2026.


“Our goal at Turtle Creek is to seek to roughly double an $800 million investment into $1.6 billion of value over the next 24 months,” said Brent Bilsland, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer. “We believe the market ascribes little to no value to the project today. Turtle Creek will diversify Hallador's generation into natural gas and make us a multi-fuel independent power producer, which we believe broadens the group of investors who can own our shares and finance our company.”


Hallador holds title to the turbines and generator equipment acquired at a substantial discount due in part to the fact that it was located in the Philippines. The equipment has been exported and is now en route to the United States, giving Hallador a speed-to-market advantage over competing projects.


The Midcontinent Independent System Operator (MISO) has completed the interconnection study, and Hallador is finalizing the engineering and construction agreement and remaining equipment purchase orders. The Company is targeting a final investment decision before year-end and is focused on securing long-term offtake agreements with investment-grade counterparties in early 2027.


Bilsland added, “Offtake contracts are the next step in building the project's value. Our financing plan does not require those contracts to be in place, but we believe long-term contracts are likely to improve the terms on which we can raise additional capital. As we advance toward our targeted commercial operation date in the second half of 2028, our objective is to build value at each development stage with little to no equity dilution.”


Each of the three major Merom offtake agreements signed this year, including the latest agreement in October, priced substantially higher than the one before it, bringing Hallador’s forward sales book to approximately $3.0 billion1, including intercompany coal sales. On a combined capacity and energy basis, the October agreement priced at over $80 per megawatt-hour, the highest in the Company’s forward sales book. These agreements pair creditworthy counterparties with protections that help preserve Hallador’s margins. Contract pricing steps up materially beginning in 2027. The Company is focused on generating more hours at Merom, bringing Turtle Creek online and turning that progress into value for shareholders.


**Turtle Creek Update**


In October 2026, Hallador took title to the turbine equipment under its $350 million asset purchase agreement with Energy World Corporation Ltd. The turbines have never been operated. The equipment departed the Philippines and is being transported to the United States, where Siemens will inspect it and bring it to current spec before installation, as is standard for relocated turbine equipment. The Company deposited the remaining $265 million of the purchase consideration into escrow, with releases tied to milestones under the agreement.


"MISO notified us that the interconnection study, which ran through MISO’s Expedited Resource Addition Study program, is complete,” said Bilsland. “We are now finalizing the interconnection agreement, which has not yet been executed. We are finalizing an engineering and construction agreement and purchase orders for the balance of the equipment. Our goal is FID before the end of 2026, and commencement of commercial operation remains targeted for the second half of 2028.”


During the quarter, Hallador entered into a $600 million senior secured construction bridge loan facility2 with a term out option to fund Turtle Creek. This loan facility represents the largest component of the project’s capital plan. The Company is also finalizing a $75 million super-priority revolving credit facility to supplement its liquidity. Hallador continues to evaluate additional financing sources to meet remaining capital requirements with a focus on structures that result in little to no equity dilution.


1 – Total Forward Sales Position as of September 30, 2026, including the impacts of the October 7, 2026 contracts. See Forward Sales Position Table below.
2 – The $600 million facility comprises $550 million funded at closing and a committed $50 million delayed draw term loan tranche, which remained undrawn at quarter-end and is available for 12 months after the closing, subject to an agreed draw schedule and funding conditions.


**Third Quarter 2026 Highlights**


- Hallador’s third quarter results improved sequentially versus the second quarter, as Merom generation increased 77% to approximately 1.4 million megawatt hours following completion of a planned major maintenance outage in July.


- While total revenue decreased 11% year-over-year to $130.3 million, primarily due to lower third-party coal sales, total revenue increased 28% quarter-over-quarter owing to higher delivered energy sales.
- Net loss was $4.5 million in Q3 2026 compared to net income of $23.9 million in the prior-year period and a net loss of $15.2 million in the second quarter of 2026. Adjusted EBITDA was $17.3 million in the third quarter of 2026 compared to $24.9 million in the prior-year period and $(2.9) million in the second quarter of 2026.


- The Company secured new construction financing to fund Turtle Creek development, while strengthening liquidity and continuing capital investment at Merom.


- Total debt rose to $551.9 million at September 30, 2026, from $45.0 million at June 30, 2026, following the closing of a $600.0 million new senior secured construction bridge loan facility and refinancing of existing debt. The facility comprises $550.0 million funded at closing and a committed $50.0 million delayed draw term loan tranche, which remained undrawn at quarter-end and is available subject to funding conditions. At quarter-end, $329.8 million of the funded proceeds remained in restricted cash, primarily for the turbine acquisition and related costs.


- Total liquidity was $103.2 million at September 30, 2026, compared to $84.2 million at June 30, 2026 and $46.4 million at September 30, 2025.


- Capital expenditures were $57.1 million in Q3 2026 compared to $19.5 million in the prior-year period, primarily driven by expenditures for the Turtle Creek project and Merom reliability upgrades completed during the planned outage.


- Hallador continues to execute its contracting strategy, increasing long-term revenue visibility and monetizing its dispatchable generation platform.


- As of September 30, 2026, and including the impacts of the agreements signed on October 7, 2026, Hallador had $2.5 billion of contracted revenue from delivered energy, accredited capacity and third-party coal sales, with accredited capacity commitments extending through 2040. Including intercompany coal sales, total contracted revenue at the segment level was $3.0 billion.

**About Hallador Energy Company**


Hallador Energy Company (Nasdaq: HNRG) is a vertically-integrated Independent Power Producer (IPP) based in Terre Haute, Indiana. The Company has two core businesses: Hallador Power Company, LLC, which produces electricity and provides accredited capacity at its one-Gigawatt (GW) Merom Generating Station, and Sunrise Coal, LLC, which produces and supplies fuel to the Merom Generating Station and other companies. Hallador is also developing Turtle Creek Gas, a 460 Megawatt (MW) natural gas generation project that will expand and diversify its generation portfolio. To learn more about Hallador, visit the Company’s website at[www.halladorenergy.com](https://www.globenewswire.com/Tracker?data=lckNljkSp3t5ZoqnmHbo2ZK24D2_dzbXBIgoJmRxIqw4doP8-DGCvbtHi29h1614uhC12QJuXRMucWvl_k6wvYLXq8HYYb3BL26Zn51Gdlw=) .
